title: Willow Creek Platform Activation — Orientation & Ops Handoff
summary: Kickoff / orientation for Redwood activation. Reviewed onboarding milestones, networking/VPC requirements, auth and KMS, low-latency targets for customer-facing features, and monitoring/alerting expectations. Decided to start with a hosted pilot for rapid validation, then move to Dedicated capacity in Q2 if latency goals hold. Agreed on next steps: share runbook, schedule network peering workshop, provide pricing for Dedicated sizing, and set a security deep-dive for SOC2/HSM questions.
action_items: Sofia Chen: Send onboarding runbook + architecture checklist by 2027-01-14
Miguel Ortega: Share sample perf benchmark workbook and sequence-length profile template by 2027-01-15
Jon Kim: Confirm VPC CIDR and firewall constraints by 2027-01-18
Laura Green: Compile list of compliance questions for SOC2 + KMS to share ahead of security deep-dive by 2027-01-20
Aisha Patel: Confirm pilot success criteria (latency p95 <= 350ms, error rate < 0.5%) by 2027-01-19
next_steps: Redwood to send runbook and example configs
Schedule 90-min network peering workshop (SE + infra) next week
Security deep-dive to be scheduled with Redwood security lead
Pilot kickoff: deploy sample model to hosted API and run smoke tests (target week of 2027-01-25)
Pricing/commit guidance for Dedicated options to be provided after perf bench results
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-12 16:00 PST | Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood CSM), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Willow Creek VP Product), Jon Kim (Willow Creek Head of Infrastructure), Rashid Al-Mansoori (Eng Manager), Laura Green (Security)

Summary: Orientation and ops handoff for activation. Talked through network, auth, pilot plan, and compliance. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Sofia Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia, I'll be your customer success lead for this activation. Miguel from our solutions eng team is here for the technical parts. Can we do quick intros?
[00:18] Aisha Patel: Hi, I'm Aisha, VP Product at Willow Creek, focused on the chat features and rollout. Excited to move fast but we also need to keep compliance tight.
[00:28] Jon Kim: Jon here, head of infra. I'll own the network side and peering.
[00:32] Rashid Al-Mansoori: Rashid, engineering manager, we'll run the integration and own the SDKs.
[00:38] Laura Green: Laura, security and compliance. I'll flag SOC2, KMS/HSM, and data residency needs.
[00:45] Miguel Ortega: Hey, Miguel from Redwood SE. I'll lead the bench and work with Jon on networking items.

[01:00] Sofia Chen: Great, goal for today is alignment on pilot scope: we want a hosted pilot to validate latency and cost, then a path to Dedicated if needed. Also cover onboarding runbook, network, and security checkpoints. Does that match everyone's expectations?
[01:18] Aisha Patel: Yes, hosted pilot first. Our product team needs p95 latency under 350ms for the user-facing assistant to feel snappy, and we want token cost visibility.
[01:28] Jon Kim: From infra, we need to understand required egress, peering options, and firewall rules. We prefer VPC peering but we need the CIDR ranges up front.

[02:00] Miguel Ortega: Quick note — our hosted mode supports secure connections over TLS; we also offer a VPC connector for private networking and Dedicated pools for reserved capacity later. For the pilot, we typically do a minimal VPC peering or NAT egress depending on customer preference.
[02:20] Jon Kim: Is VPC peering available in your hosted offering or that's only for Private? I might be mixing terms.
[02:28] Miguel Ortega: Good question — sorry for the jargon. Hosted API: standard public endpoints with strong encryption and customer-level isolation. We support VPC connector options that enable traffic to exit into a customer-managed VPC for some customers; Dedicated and Private have deeper network isolation. For the pilot, we can do secure public endpoints and optionally set up a peering workshop to evaluate a connector.

[03:05] Laura Green: On the security front: we need to confirm KMS integration for key management, whether we can bring our own key (BYOK) or HSM, and retention for logs and request payloads. Also SSO for the console and RBAC.
[03:22] Miguel Ortega: We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has envelope encryption and can integrate with KMS for enterprise tiers — we'll detail that in the security doc. Console SSO via SAML/SSO is available for enterprise workspaces.
[03:40] Sofia Chen: I'll put the security doc link in the notes after the call — it covers SOC2, encryption, and audit logs.

[04:05] Aisha Patel: Useful — another constraint: a portion of our data needs to stay in region eu-west-1 for regulatory reasons. How flexible are you on region pinning for the pilot?
[04:18] Miguel Ortega: We can pin workloads to regions where Redwood operates. For hosted, we have nodes in NA and EU regions; for strict residency, Dedicated or Private is better. For the pilot, EU region deployment is possible if you want to test latency from your users in EMEA.

[05:00] Rashid Al-Mansoori: On the integration side, we're planning to use the SDK for streaming responses. We need to confirm kv cache behavior and how to persist conversation context across restarts. Also how session tokens rotate.
[05:18] Miguel Ortega: Our runtime manages KV caches in-memory per replica and supports checkpointing for longer sessions via optional persistent cache layers. For streaming, we support chunked tokens and resumable streams — we'll share the developer notes.

[06:00] Jon Kim: Can we run a quick perf test with 2K concurrent users hitting short prompts to see tail latency? What's the recommended sequence length for benching?
[06:12] Miguel Ortega: Recommend sampling from real traffic — but for a baseline use 32–128 token prompts. We'll provide a perf workbook. For 2K concurrency we typically recommend mixing batching configs and the Dedicated path; but we'll run hosted pilot to collect real seq-length distributions.

[07:00] Sofia Chen: OK we'll make that an action item: Miguel shares the sample perf workbook and a template for sequence-length profiling.

[07:20] Aisha Patel: Timeline question: we want pilot results before end of January and aim for a production roll in mid-March. Is that feasible?
[07:28] Sofia Chen: That aligns — pilot kickoff next week, two-week validation, and then iterate. Mid-March seems doable if perf and security checks pass.

[08:00] Laura Green: SOC2 — are you SOC2 compliant now? We need documentation for our audit. Also any third-party subprocessors list.
[08:12] Miguel Ortega: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant; I'll link the attestation and the subprocessor list. For deeper questions on HSM/BYOK we'll set a security deep-dive with our security lead.

[09:00] Jon Kim: On networking specifics: we need a list of IP ranges and endpoints to allow through our firewall, or a peering guide if we go that route. Also details about TLS ciphers and mutual TLS support.
[09:18] Miguel Ortega: We'll provide an IP/endpoint allowlist and a peering playbook. Mutual TLS isn't on by default for hosted public endpoints, but Dedicated/Private can support mTLS. We'll capture your preference in the workshop.

[10:00] Rashid Al-Mansoori: For rollout strategy, we want canary traffic to start at 1% and ramp. Does Redwood support canary route control and automatic fallback?
[10:12] Miguel Ortega: Yes — Redwood Console supports rollout policies, canary rules, and automatic fallback to a previous model variant on error thresholds. We can demo that during the handoff.

[12:00] Sofia Chen: Quick note — I'm going to share the onboarding runbook now. It has an architecture checklist, roles, success criteria, and a sample sprint plan. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/willow-creek-activation (note: placeholder).

[13:00] Aisha Patel: Thanks. On cost: rough run-rate numbers would help. We need to decide whether we take reserved Dedicated credits or keep hosted pay-as-you-go depending on pilot results.
[13:18] Miguel Ortega: We'll provide a cost model after the perf bench is run. Dedicated gives cost predictability at commit tiers; hosted is flexible with unit cost visibility in the Console.

[14:30] Laura Green: For logs and telemetry — retention windows and access controls? We need to be able to export audit logs to our SIEM and set retention to 365 days for certain trails.
[14:45] Miguel Ortega: Audit logs can be streamed to customer destinations (SIEM, S3) on enterprise plans. Retention policies vary by plan; we'll surface options in the security doc and runbook.

[16:00] Jon Kim: Are there known limitations around model sizes or quantized variants that affect latency predictions?
[16:12] Miguel Ortega: Model size and quantization definitely affect perf. For large context models, KV cache size and attention optimizations are key. We'll suggest model variants and quantization profiles in the recommendation doc.

[18:00] Sofia Chen: Let's capture success criteria one more time: Aisha — lat p95 <= 350ms, error rate < 0.5%, cost per 1k tokens within target budget. Anything to add?
[18:18] Aisha Patel: Also need feature parity for streaming and the function-calling layer for tool integrations.

[19:00] Miguel Ortega: Noted. We'll include functional smoke tests for streaming and function-call behavior in the bench.

[21:00] Laura Green: On legal/contracting — who should our procurement contact? We'll want a standard enterprise contract with data processing addendum.
[21:18] Sofia Chen: I'll follow up with procurement contact details and attach a sample DPA and SOW templates.

[23:00] Rashid Al-Mansoori: For the integration plan, we'll need sample code for retries and idempotency keys — sometimes the client side needs guidance on handling partial streams.
[23:18] Miguel Ortega: We'll share SDK best practices and a snippet for idempotency keys, retry strategy, and ephemeral token rotation.

[25:00] Aisha Patel: Any gotchas we should be aware of from other customers?
[25:12] Miguel Ortega: Common issues: not sampling real sequence lengths which skews batching, forgetting to pin region for residency, and underestimating cold-starts for certain model variants. We'll point these out in the runbook.

[28:00] Sofia Chen: Okay, let's lock next steps — workshop dates, docs, and next meeting.
[28:12] Jon Kim: I'm available next Thursday for a 90-min network workshop.
[28:20] Miguel Ortega: I'll propose times for next Thursday and Friday.

[30:00] Laura Green: For the security deep-dive, please include your security lead and relevant folks from infra. 60–90 minutes should be fine.
[30:12] Sofia Chen: We'll schedule that the week after the perf bench.

[32:00] Aisha Patel: Quick question for SE: how do you handle model upgrades — automatic or manual? We want staged upgrades with rollbacks.
[32:12] Miguel Ortega: Staged by default in the Console; we support canary phases and automatic rollback thresholds. You get per-route dashboards and tracing to track regressions.

[35:00] Rashid Al-Mansoori: We'll need training for our devs — is there a sandbox for devs to play with?
[35:12] Sofia Chen: Yes — dev sandbox and tutorial labs. We'll include access in the runbook and set up a short training session after the pilot results.

[38:00] Aisha Patel: Regarding metrics — we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards to present to execs.
[38:12] Miguel Ortega: Console provides token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, and traces. We can build a dashboard and share CSV exports.

[40:00] Sofia Chen: Recap of assigned owners: Miguel will share perf workbook; Sofia will send runbook and procurement docs; Jon will confirm network CIDR; Laura compiles security Qs; Aisha will finalize success criteria.

[41:00] Miguel Ortega: I'll also include a sample benchmark that mimics chat traffic and a sequence-length capture script.

[45:00] Aisha Patel: I appreciate the clarity. Any blockers we foresee?
[45:12] Jon Kim: Only the CIDR and a short firewall window for the perf test. Once we have the IP lists it's straightforward.

[48:00] Laura Green: We'll want the SOC2 and subprocessor docs before the pilot — otherwise we can't proceed with sensitive data tests.
[48:12] Sofia Chen: Understood — we'll prioritize sharing those docs.

[50:00] Rashid Al-Mansoori: Slightly off topic — what's the support model during pilot? On-call SLA?
[50:12] Miguel Ortega: For pilots, we provide priority SE support during scheduled tests. For production we have tiered SLAs; we'll include suggested on-call rotations in the runbook.

[55:00] Sofia Chen: Let's do a quick recap and confirm dates: runbook and perf workbook this week, network workshop next Thursday, security deep-dive week after, pilot kick week of Jan 25, aim for production mid-March. Agreed?
[55:18] Aisha Patel: Agreed.
[55:24] Jon Kim: Agreed.
[55:28] Laura Green: Agreed, pending SOC2 docs.

[58:00] Sofia Chen: Great — I'll email the notes, action items, and the runbook links. Expect the runbook and perf template by Friday.
[58:18] Miguel Ortega: I'll get the benchmark workbook ready and the endpoint/IP allowlist.

[60:00] Aisha Patel: Thanks — excited to get started.
[60:06] Sofia Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and doc links. Bye.
[60:12] (call ends)
